free_tier.stated: No account, no total quota — per-object only. '1ファイル最大128 GiB。複数ファイルも順番にアップロードできます' (max 128 GiB per file, multiple files uploaded in sequence). Upload form constant `data-max="137438953472"` = 128 GiB, confirming the number in the markup.

retention.stated: per-object-cap 128 GiB. Retention is client-chosen (published-until field showed 'No limit' on a live file) and additionally bounded by a download-count cap the uploader may set

egress.terms: No egress meter or paid bandwidth product; the whole service is stated free ('本サービスは、別途明示する場合を除き無料です').

tooling: No public API and no rclone backend — form-POST only, behind a Laravel CSRF token (`_token`) plus a session cookie, with `delpass` (delete key, >=8 chars) and optional `expiry_datetime`/`maxcount`. The legacy numbered URLs (`/u/4144979`) still resolve; new uploads get random `/u/f_<22-char>` URLs.
chaining: Account-less: unlimited objects per IP x 128 GiB each, with 'No limit' available as the expiry. Chain is a re-upload loop only if you set an expiry; with expiry unset the object has no scheduled deletion.
limits_note: per-object-cap 128 GiB. Retention is client-chosen (published-until field showed 'No limit' on a live file) and additionally bounded by a download-count cap the uploader may set. Read path is POST-only: `GET /download` returns 405 with `Allow: POST`, and a correctly-tokened POST 302s back to the share page — so a bytes-fetching client must follow the browser's two-step handshake, which is exactly the upload-open/read-gated pattern the brief warns about.

reliability_note: This is the legendary Japanese uploader and it is emphatically alive: the public file list was showing uploads from minutes earlier on the day of this run. But it has already had at least one near-death outage that lost voicebanks (UTAU Wiki recorded the site going dark and coming back with a broken certificate), and its own terms say no-expiry is 'not a promise of permanent storage'. Treat it as a live service with a history of vanishing.
